questions: What does the array P represent: is P_i the bib number of the person that person i is staring at, or something else?
What does the array Q represent: is Q_i the bib number of person i, or does Q map bib numbers to people?
Are the bib numbers guaranteed to be a permutation of 1..N, or can they be any distinct integers within the range?
Should the output be a single line of N integers separated by spaces, or one integer per line, or some other format?
In what order should the results be printed: for i = 1..N, or in the order of bib numbers, or according to the input arrays?
If a person is staring at themselves (i.e., P_i = i), is that allowed, and how should it be handled?
Are there any constraints on the relationship between P and Q (e.g., can they be independent permutations), or must they satisfy a specific condition?
What should be done if the input violates the stated constraints (e.g., duplicate values), is undefined behavior acceptable, or must an error be reported?

inline_prompts: There are N people numbered from 1 to N. Related — "person i" is the i-th person, which bears on what P_i represents. For each i = 1,2,\ldots,N, find the number written on the bib of the person that the person wearing the bib with number i is staring at. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N P_1 P_2 \dots P_N Q_1 Q_2 \dots Q_N Output Print the result. Constraints - 2 \leq N \leq 3\times 10^5 - 1 \leq P_i \leq N - The values of P_i are distinct. - 1 \leq Q_i \leq N - The values of Q_i are distinct. - All input values are integers.
